transcript.content: Hello, I’m Dr. ____. What brings you in today?

I’m here because I feel like I’m always running hot, you know? Like I can’t shut the motor off. And lately, that’s been getting me in trouble at the firehouse. Which is crazy because I love the guys there. We had this chili cook-off last weekend, actually, and I swear Henderson put ghost peppers in his batch just to mess with me. I was sweating through my shirt for an hour. But yeah, anyway, the captain pulled me aside yesterday and said I need to get a handle on things because I'm just constantly pacing around the rigs when we're supposed to be on downtime. I just... I can't just sit in the recliner and watch TV with the rest of them. My legs start twitching if I sit for more than five minutes.
Do you find yourself worrying a lot, even when there isn’t an obvious reason to?

Worrying? No, not really. I mean, I don't sit around chewing my nails or stressing out over nothing. If there's a problem, I just want to do something about it, you know? 

Like, we got this call last Tuesday for a cat stuck in a tree. Classic, right? You’d think people don’t actually call the station for that anymore, but this lady down on 4th street has this massive oak tree in her front yard. Beautiful tree, honestly. I’ve been thinking about planting an oak in my backyard, but the soil there is so clay-heavy, I don't know if the roots would take. I bought this aerator tool from Home Depot a few weeks ago to try and fix the lawn, but I lost the receipt and it's just sitting in my garage next to my old dirt bike. I really need to sell that bike, the carburetor is completely shot and I just never get around to it... 

Wait, what were we talking about? Sorry. But yeah, worrying... no, I don't really get anxious or anything like that.
Have you had this kind of difficulty staying focused or getting organized since childhood?

Oh, yeah, definitely. My mom says I was exactly like this back in grade school too. She always reminds me how I was constantly out of my seat, blurting out answers, losing my homework... just a total handful. She used to get all these notes sent home from my teachers saying I was bright enough to do the work, but I just wouldn't settle down. 

She actually kept a bunch of those notes in this old shoebox. I saw it when I was helping her clean out her garage last summer. Man, her garage was a complete disaster. She had this old riding mower in there that hasn't run since like 2015. I told her I could probably fix it if I just cleaned the spark plugs and checked the fuel line, but you know how it is, trying to find the time. Plus, I usually just use a push mower for my yard anyway. It's better cardio, and honestly, I need it. I try to get a run in on my off days, but my left knee has been acting up ever since we had to haul all this heavy gear up three flights of stairs during a drill last month. 

Wait, what did you ask me? Sorry. Oh, right, childhood. But yeah, my mom says I've basically always been this way.
Have you ever been diagnosed with a thyroid problem?

Thyroid? No, not that I know of. My physicals for the department always come back clean, mostly. They're pretty strict about checking our bloodwork and all that, you know, because of the smoke exposure. Actually, my buddy Dave—he drives the tiller truck—he just found out he has high cholesterol and they put him on this crazy strict diet. Poor guy can't even look at a cheeseburger anymore. We used to hit up this diner on 5th Avenue after a long shift, they make these incredible patty melts. You know the kind with the rye bread and the caramelized onions? I tried making them at home once, but I burnt the onions. I always get impatient and turn the heat up too high. I just can't stand standing there stirring for twenty minutes. It's like, who has the time? I ended up just ordering a pizza instead. The pizza place near me has this really good hot honey pepperoni... 

Anyway, what were you asking? Oh, thyroid. No, I don't think so. Never been told I have a problem with it.
Do you spend a lot of time worrying that there is something seriously wrong with your health?

Worry about my health? No, not really. Like I said, the department keeps pretty close tabs on us anyway, so I figure if something was wrong, they'd catch it. I feel fine, mostly. I mean, besides that knee thing I mentioned. 

I actually tried using the rowing machine at the station yesterday to take it easy on the joints, but the digital monitor on it is totally busted. It just flashes 88:88 constantly. It's so distracting. I told the captain we should just order a new one, maybe one of those fancy ones with the water resistance? I saw a commercial for those when I was up late the other night. I couldn't sleep because my neighbor's dog wouldn't stop barking. It's this little terrier mix—cute, but man, it has a set of lungs on it. I almost went over there to say something, but it was like 2 AM, and I didn't want to be that guy, you know? Plus, I had to be up at 5 for a shift anyway, so I just put on a podcast to drown it out. It was this really interesting one about how they used to build ships in the 1700s, with all the tar and the wood bending... 

Wait, sorry, what did you ask me? I totally lost my train of thought. Oh, right, worrying about getting sick. Yeah, no, I don't really stress about that kind of stuff at all.
Did you have these same attention or restlessness problems in more than one setting, like at home and at school or work?

Yeah, I guess it's pretty much everywhere. Like I said, at school I was always getting in trouble for being out of my seat, and at home my mom was always on my case about my room being a disaster or me not finishing my chores. Even now at the firehouse, the guys are always giving me grief because I start cleaning the rig, and then I notice a loose bolt on the ladder, so I go get the toolbox, but then I see the air tanks need refilling, and next thing you know, the rig is half-washed, the toolbox is sitting out, and I'm off doing something else. 

It's actually kind of funny, my buddy Dave—the one with the cholesterol—he calls me the "Tasmanian Devil" because I just blow through a room and leave a trail of half-finished projects. Speaking of Dave, he actually brought in these turkey burgers the other day to try and stick to his diet, and they were... well, they were terrible. Dry as a bone. I felt bad for the guy, so I tried to show him how to mix in some Greek yogurt and a little bit of feta cheese to keep them moist. I saw that trick on a cooking show once. It was one of those weekend marathon things, you know? They had this whole segment on grilling, and they showed how to make these cedar-plank salmon fillets that looked amazing. I actually bought some cedar planks to try it, but they're still sitting in my trunk. I keep forgetting to bring them inside. My trunk is a mess right now, honestly. I've got my turnout gear, my gym bag, the cedar planks, and like three empty water bottles rolling around in there. 

What were we talking about? Oh, right, the attention stuff. But yeah, it's definitely not just at work or just at home. It's kind of a full-time thing for me.

He reports chronic restlessness, inability to stay seated, pacing, fidgeting/leg twitching, blurting out answers as a child, losing homework, distractibility, disorganization, unfinished tasks, and symptoms at school, home, and work causing occupational problems. There is no evidence that anxiety, thyroid disease, or another medical condition better explains the presentation.
